title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 to a cryptocurrency scam that used a fake AI-generated website to display false investment information. The scammer initiated contact via WhatsApp and directed the victim to a legitimate mobile trading app, then presented fraudulent account statements through a fabricated site that made the illicit transactions appear genuine. The deception built trust through small, withdrawable gains before escalating to larger sums.

This is a case of impersonation and visual fraud in the presentation layer of a financial system. The deployed AI technology, image generation, was used not by the legitimate trading app but by the attacker to create a false interface showing account balances and gains that never existed. The failure was not in the app itself but in the victim's inability to verify the authenticity of what appeared on his screen against the actual records held by the financial institution.

It is not established whether the trading app had security features that could have alerted the user to the deception, or whether additional verification steps at the point of withdrawal could have exposed the scam before such large losses occurred.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest using a mobile trading app, initially allowing him to make small trades and withdraw money to build trust. Over time, the investments grew larger, but when Jerry tried to withdraw more funds recently, he discovered the scam. Police determined that while the app itself was legitimate, scammers had created a fake AI-generated site that showed false investment information on his screen.

The couple, Jerry and Mindy Dunaway, say they are angry and embarrassed but want to warn others about the sophisticated tactics criminals use. Though they are working with Gwinnett County police, investigators say victims in these cases rarely recover their money. Their children have started a GoFundMe page to help the family pay everyday expenses while they work to rebuild their lives.
